title: You’ve Got Mail! The Late 19th Century U.S. Postal Service Expansion, Firm Creation, and Firm Performance
eligible_reason: Cross-sectional long-difference design, not a panel DiD. entry_ind_dun_l.dta has one row per city x industry (40,827 rows) with ihs_growth_8090 = growth in businesses 1880-1890 regressed on dum_po20SRSN (new post office 1880-1890 within 20 km) with county and industry FE (Tables 1-4: reghdfe ihs_growth_8090 dum_po20SRSN [controls], absorb(county_id industry_id)); Table 2 instruments the post office with a post-route change (ivreghdfe, logit first stage); Table 3 interacts with continuous moderators. Tables 5-7 (performance_l.dta, firm cross-section) are probit/OLS of 1880-1890 performance changes. No unit x period panel, no calendar-time FE, no staggered adoption dates.
design_notes: Stata 18 reghdfe/ivreghdfe/probit; entry_final.do (Tables 1-4), performance_final.do (Tables 5-7). Treatment local pos = dum_po20SRSN; controls ln_tot_biz_city_1880 lnpop_80 rail10 river10. Clustering city_county_id.
data_files_note: README.txt: all data necessary to reproduce the main tables are included, de-identified (R.G. Dun & Co. credit reports, Harvard Library).
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Long-difference cross-section with IV; no DiD panel.
